title: Lipid profile
subtitle: Total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, triglycerides for cardiovascular risk assessment
summary: Lipid panel measurement for cardiovascular risk assessment and monitoring of statin therapy.
introduction: Interpret total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, non-HDL and triglycerides with established CVD, inherited disease and overall risk. Routine risk assessment may use non-fasting profiles; selected high-triglyceride investigations require fasting. Follow the reporting laboratory’s service instructions: Belfast biochemistry manual rev18 specifies 14-hour fasting for its triglyceride entry, which needs reconciliation with the clinical indication/local workflow.

rows.name: Total cholesterol
rows.referenceRange: Interpret with non-HDL, LDL, indication and overall CVD risk; a descriptive cholesterol band is not a prescribing threshold.
lowInterpretation: The lipid contribution is favourable; overall risk and treatment need depend on established disease, age, blood pressure, diabetes, CKD, smoking, inherited disease and current treatment.
highInterpretation: Assess the full profile, family history, overall risk and secondary causes; use the indication-specific prevention/FH pathway rather than total cholesterol alone.
notes: Non-HDL cholesterol = total cholesterol − HDL cholesterol.
Total cholesterol ≈ LDL + HDL + triglycerides/2.2 is the rearranged Friedewald estimate in mmol/L, not a universal measured identity. Follow the laboratory’s calculation/reporting limits.

rows.name: LDL cholesterol
rows.referenceRange: Targets depend on indication. NICE secondary prevention: LDL ≤2.0 mmol/L or non-HDL ≤2.6 mmol/L. Primary prevention assesses treatment response, including >40% non-HDL reduction under NICE NG238.
lowInterpretation: The lipid contribution is favourable; overall risk and treatment need depend on established disease, age, blood pressure, diabetes, CKD, smoking, inherited disease and current treatment.
highInterpretation: Raised LDL needs assessment through the appropriate prevention or FH pathway. Choose treatment and additional agents by indication, response, tolerance and eligibility; LDL >4.1 mmol/L alone is not a universal escalation rule.
notes: Use the locally adopted LDL reporting limits and treatment pathway.

Calculated LDL may be unavailable/unreliable with raised triglycerides; use non-HDL or suitable laboratory-directed direct assessment when the calculation is invalid. Do not mix alternative formula limits.

rows.name: HDL cholesterol
rows.referenceRange: Interpret HDL with the full lipid profile and overall risk; it is not an independent treatment target.
lowInterpretation: Lower HDL can accompany increased risk, but treatment decisions require the complete clinical risk assessment. Encourage healthy activity, weight management and smoking cessation as appropriate.
highInterpretation: HDL is one risk marker, not a treatment target or guarantee of protection. Very high HDL may not be protective; assess other risk factors. Do not recommend alcohol to raise HDL.
notes: HDL is one risk marker, not a treatment target or guarantee of protection. Very high HDL may not be protective; assess other risk factors. Do not recommend alcohol to raise HDL.

rows.name: Triglycerides
rows.referenceRange: Use reporting-laboratory interval and staged clinical review: 4.5–9.9, 10–20 and >20 mmol/L have different assessment actions.
lowInterpretation: The lipid contribution is favourable; overall risk and treatment need depend on established disease, age, blood pressure, diabetes, CKD, smoking, inherited disease and current treatment.
highInterpretation: For triglycerides 4.5–9.9 mmol/L, optimise CVD risk and secondary causes; risk tools may underestimate risk. For 10–20 mmol/L, repeat fasting after at least 5 days and within 2 weeks, assess secondary causes and seek specialist advice if >10 persists. For >20 mmol/L not explained by excess alcohol or poor glycaemic control, arrange urgent specialist review through the adopted pathway. Pancreatitis symptoms require acute hospital assessment regardless of the band.

Review diabetes/glycaemic control, alcohol, obesity, medicines, thyroid/renal disease and other secondary causes. Fibrate choice and very-low-fat diets require clinical/dietetic/specialist assessment; avoid routine omega-3 or automatic fibrate treatment from a single band.
notes: A physiological post-meal rise is not an assay false positive. Confirm when fasting is requested and follow the local collection instruction.

Use local LDL calculation/reporting limits and non-HDL or suitable direct lipid assessment if invalid. Suspected pseudohyponatraemia requires sodium by direct ion-selective electrode (often a blood-gas analyser), not direct LDL/apoB.
Marked triglyceride elevation can be secondary or inherited; a concentration alone is not an automatic genetic-testing indication.

commonPatterns.title: Favourable lipid contribution within overall risk assessment
interpretation: The lipid contribution is favourable; overall risk and treatment need depend on established disease, age, blood pressure, diabetes, CKD, smoking, inherited disease and current treatment.
Current treatment may explain favourable levels and may remain indicated.
actions: Counsel on diet, exercise, weight management and smoking cessation as appropriate.
Plan risk-appropriate follow-up; do not mandate annual universal lipid screening for all favourable profiles.

commonPatterns.title: Raised atherogenic cholesterol: assess indication and causes
findings: Raised LDL and/or non-HDL relative to the appropriate indication/response target
Assess other risk factors, personal/family CVD and secondary causes
interpretation: Lipid treatment requires an indication-specific assessment; the profile alone is not a universal drug rule.

Offer/optimise lipid-lowering treatment through the appropriate primary-/secondary-prevention or FH pathway.
Assess diet, activity, weight, smoking, medicines, alcohol, renal function and glycaemic status; thyroid testing when clinically indicated.

commonPatterns.title: Marked triglyceride elevation
findings: Raised triglycerides interpreted by staged review
Assess symptoms, secondary causes and relevant family history
interpretation: Pancreatitis risk and CVD assessment require clinical context; secondary causes are common.
actions: For triglycerides 4.5–9.9 mmol/L, optimise CVD risk and secondary causes; risk tools may underestimate risk. For 10–20 mmol/L, repeat fasting after at least 5 days and within 2 weeks, assess secondary causes and seek specialist advice if >10 persists. For >20 mmol/L not explained by excess alcohol or poor glycaemic control, arrange urgent specialist review through the adopted pathway. Pancreatitis symptoms require acute hospital assessment regardless of the band.
Review and address alcohol, glycaemic control, obesity, medicines, thyroid/renal disease; involve a dietitian/specialist for severe disease.
Choose fibrate or other treatment only through the adopted specialist/local pathway; genetic assessment depends on the complete phenotype/family history.

rationale: Review full lipid profile and liver transaminases about 2–3 months after treatment initiation or change, then risk-/treatment-appropriate ongoing review. Use the high-triglyceride pathway for timely fasting confirmation rather than routine annual-only review.
Assess renal function, glycaemia, liver transaminases, medicines and alcohol before treatment as appropriate; check thyroid function when clinically indicated. Use the local lipid/statin pathway.

Use Simon Broome/DLCN clinical criteria and specialist-directed FH genetic/cascade assessment when indicated. FH testing concerns appropriate genes such as LDLR/APOB/PCSK9; HFE is an iron-overload test.

specimens.notes: Confirm the current local lipid-profile tube, volume and handling with the reporting laboratory. Routine national CVD assessment may be non-fasting; Belfast biochemistry manual rev18 p93 specifies 14-hour fasting for triglycerides. Reconcile the requested test/clinical indication with that local service instruction, especially for high-TG follow-up.
